Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

at once adverb

also right away, immediately, right now

classical

Plaut.
Ter.

āctūtum

Other words

  • statim — at once, immediately

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.55 (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.53 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87: immediately, statim, continuō; Traupman 331

    The ordinary word of classical prose; Lewis & Short finds āctūtum above all in Plautus, and hardly in classical prose.

  • continuō — at once, immediately, forthwith

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 3.1.7: quae ut aspexī, mē continuō contulī (Lewis & Short s.v. continuus); Traupman 106: right away, continuō; Traupman 331

    What follows straight on something else: “very frequent in all periods”, Lewis & Short.

  • nuncjam — right now, now at last

    adverb, nunc and jam · also used · classical · Traupman 107: right now, nunciam; Lewis & Short s.v. nunc, referring to jam

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Traupman prints nunciam; with consonantal j the house spelling is nuncjam. Lewis & Short has no entry of its own for the word and sends the reader to jam.

  • prōtinus — right away, straightaway

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. prōtinus: immediately, at once; Traupman 162

  • extemplō — immediately, in an instant

    also used · classical · Traupman 331

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; et in historiīs)

Examples

  • «Agedum,» inquit pater, «onerā palliolō umerōs tuōs, et āctūtum sequere mē.»

    “Come on,” said Dad, “put your little coat on your shoulders and follow me at once.”Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

See also hurry up!, now.
